question_text:
Which of the following statements are true and which are false? Give reasons for your answers.
(i) Only one line can pass through a single point.
(ii) There are an infinite number of lines which pass through two distinct points.
(iii) A terminated line can be produced indefinitely on both the sides.
(iv) If two circles are equal, then their radii are equal.
(v) In the following figure, if AB = PQ and PQ = XY, then AB = XY.

parts.part_text: Only one line can pass through a single point.
parts.answer_text: False. Since through a single point, infinite number of lines can pass.

parts.part_text: There are an infinite number of lines which pass through two distinct points.
parts.answer_text: False. Since through two distinct points, only one line can pass.

parts.part_text: A terminated line can be produced indefinitely on both the sides.
parts.answer_text: True. A terminated line can be produced indefinitely on both the sides.

parts.part_text: If two circles are equal, then their radii are equal.
parts.answer_text: True. If two circles are equal, then their centre and circumference will coincide and hence, the radii will also be equal.

parts.part_text: If AB = PQ and PQ = XY, then AB = XY.
parts.answer_text: True. It is given that AB and XY are two terminated lines and both are equal to a third line PQ. Euclid’s first axiom states that things which are equal to the same thing are equal to one another.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, the lines AB and XY will be equal to each other.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of basic geometric principles and definitions.

question_text: Consider the two ‘postulates’ given below: (i) Given any two distinct points A and B, there exists a third point C, which is between A and B. (ii) There exists at least three points that are not on the same line. Do these postulates contain any undefined terms? Are these postulates consistent? Do they follow from Euclid’s postulates? Explain.

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to the postulates.

answer_text: There are various undefined terms in the given postulates. The given postulates are consistent because they refer to two different situations. Also, it is impossible to deduce any statement that contradicts any well known axiom and postulate. These postulates do not follow from Euclid’s postulates. They follow from the axiom, 'Given two distinct points, there is a unique line that passes through them'.
final_answer: Thus, the postulates contain undefined terms and are consistent but do not follow from Euclid's postulates.

question_text: If a point C lies between two points A and B such that AC = BC, then prove that AC + AC = AB. Explain by drawing the figure.

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to the proof of the midpoint.

answer_text: It is given that, AC = BC. (Equals are added on both sides) … (1) Here, (BC + AC) coincides with AB. It is known that things which coincide with one another are equal to one another. BC + AC = AB … (2) It is also known that things which are equal to the same thing are equal to one another. Therefore, from equations (1) and (2), we obtain AC + AC = AB, which simplifies to 2AC = AB.

steps.description: Start with the given equality AC = BC.
Add AC to both sides to form BC + AC = AB.
Use the property of equality to conclude AC + AC = AB.

final_answer: Thus, it is proved that AC + AC = AB.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of equality and basic geometric properties.

question_text: How would you rewrite Euclid’s fifth postulate so that it would be easier to understand?

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to Euclid's fifth postulate.

answer_text: Two lines are said to be parallel if they are equidistant from one another and they do not have any point of intersection. In order to understand it easily, let us take any line l and a point P not on l. Then, by Playfair’s axiom (equivalent to the fifth postulate), there is a unique line m through P which is parallel to l. The distance of a point from a line is the length of the perpendicular from the point to the line. Let AB be the distance of any point on m from l and CD be the distance of any point on l from m. It can be observed that AB = CD. In this way, the distance will be the same for any point on m from l and any point on l from m. Therefore, these two lines are everywhere equidistant from one another.
final_answer: Therefore, these two lines are everywhere equidistant from one another.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of Euclid's postulate and its implications.

question_text: Does Euclid’s fifth postulate imply the existence of parallel lines? Explain.

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to the existence of parallel lines.

answer_text: Yes. According to Euclid’s 5th postulate, when a line falls on l and m and if the angles formed are less than two right angles, the lines l and m will never intersect each other. Therefore, it can be said that the lines are parallel.
final_answer: Therefore, it can be said that the lines are parallel.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of Euclid's postulate and its implications.
